# Appeal of Denial — Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**Member:** Quinn Jennings
**Member ID:** W670697505
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Georgia
**Denial date:** 2026-08-04
**Reference number:** POC-6E16FAD700-45453
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html; last review 12/11/2025)

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which was denied on 2026-08-04 for "incomplete documentation" (reference number POC-6E16FAD700-45453). My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in Aetna's possession show that I meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery. I am asking that Aetna reconsider this denial in light of the information below.

## Why I believe I meet the plan's criteria

Aetna's policy, CPB 0629, states that it "considers the following interventions medically necessary" for:

> "Members with clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management who meet the following criteria:"

and describes the covered procedure as:

> "Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:"

I am [age/DOB placeholder — please confirm from chart] years old, and my records reflect a diagnosis of symptomatic hallux valgus, so I believe this threshold requirement is met.

The policy further requires:

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

and, in a related provision:

> "Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:"

My records show the following conservative treatment, all under the direction of a healthcare professional:

- **24 months** of progressive foot pain, unrelieved by rest, documented as the underlying symptom duration.
- **NSAIDs for 6 months** with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection** on 2026-03-25, which the policy lists as a conservative measure ("Corticosteroid injections;"), giving only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Physical therapy, activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic** over 10 weeks (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21), 18 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Ongoing difficulty walking and inability to tolerate closed shoes, with ulceration risk over the bony prominence.
- Weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-29 showing a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- Exam findings of positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side.

I understand the policy also lists "Protective cushions/pads;" and "Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions;" among conservative measures. I do not see these specifically documented in the packet, and I have asked my surgeon's office to confirm whether either was tried or considered, or to explain why they were not applicable [placeholder — to be confirmed by provider]. I note the policy states that "Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded);" are treated separately from other conservative measures; my records do show a custom orthotic was used regardless.

Taken together, I believe the record shows more than six months of conservative treatment under professional direction, with persistent pain and documented difficulty walking, consistent with the policy language quoted above.

I also want to flag that several of the criteria the denial referenced — the requirement of "Minimum follow-up was at least 12 months," and the provisions concerning arthrodesis ("Another indication for arthrodesis includes a failed Keller bunionectomy," and "Fusion is the procedure of choice for hallux valgus associated with advanced degenerative joint disease, and advanced hallux valgus (IMA greater than 20 degrees, HVA greater than 40 degrees)...") — appear to relate to fusion/arthrodesis procedures or post-surgical outcome tracking, not to the bony correction bunionectomy (CPT 28296) that was requested. My imaging shows an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees and a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees, both below the "IMA greater than 20 degrees, HVA greater than 40 degrees" threshold the policy describes for fusion. I ask that Aetna confirm which criteria set applies to the procedure actually requested.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Aetna to reconsider this denial and to approve the requested bunionectomy (CPT 28296), or to specify exactly what additional documentation is needed to complete the medical necessity review, since the stated reason for denial was incomplete documentation rather than a finding that the criteria were not met.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-01-31**. I will submit this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form through my account at aetna.com, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379, and I will confirm the correct mailing address against the one printed on my denial letter before sending.

Please let me know if any additional records from Dr. Duval's office or my physical therapy provider would help complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
Date: [date of signing]
Phone: [phone number]
Email: [email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
